correctness.rationale: The six supporting planes give first feet ±q_i/κ_i, forming the asserted linear cross-polytope. Its eight facet planes have normals Cε at offset 1, so the second feet are Cε/||Cε||². The eight feet are distinct; if the hull is a parallelepiped then all are vertices, and symmetry forces its center to be zero. Four parity-class representatives span dimension three and have unique relation with coefficients s_j>0. Any parallelepiped's four antipodal pairs can be signed to satisfy a relation with all coefficients of modulus one, so uniqueness makes the s_j equal. For the norm-variance computation, it is the three length-four columns (η_ji η_jk)_j that have zero mean and are mutually orthogonal, with squared length four; this gives the asserted factor 16. Thus vanishing is exactly orthogonality of the A columns, and in that case the second pedal is the constant radial rescaling C[-1,1]^3/s_1. This checks all real invertible A without assuming the feet lie in their facets or assuming eight vertices a priori. The shear example has (11,3,3,11) and variance sum 64. The finite script was inspected, not executed.
